title: C1512 — Knock sensor 1 (KS1) connector
introduction:
I read this knock-sensor reference as a matched pair of connections. The cavity labels lead to separate circuit rows, and the full Function wording keeps each connection's identity intact. Those small suffixes earn their space: treating the pair as anonymous wires would throw away useful information before any diagnosis begins.

Start with the connector identity table, use the face drawing to find the matching cavity row, then consult the terminal and pigtail references for their respective hardware listings. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are unspecified. This is a wiring-reading guide; sensor access, probing, operating checks and replacement require the applicable separate procedure.

Read each cavity row across its circuit identifier, wire-color code, gauge entry, full function and terminal listing. Keep the bank-or-unique wording and the minus or plus suffix attached to the corresponding row. Those suffixes distinguish the paired sensor connections; a minus label alone does not establish a chassis-ground connection, and neither row supplies a test voltage or a sensor-health conclusion.
